intent: Establish a symmetric five-sensor baseline with forward-placed sensors spanning the tape width, so the Integrator can tune a controller and report how the geometry behaves. Next iterations should adjust sensor lateral spread and forward offset, track width, and mass based on observed line loss and oscillation.
learning: No prior evidence. Hypotheses: (1) a forward sensor offset of about 0.04 m reduces oscillation; (2) a wider sensor spread reduces line-loss events on tight bends; (3) a smaller mass and shorter wheel track speed up completion within 3 s. Test each by changing one variable at a time.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry and no integration feedback yet, so this is a neutral baseline rather than a tuned design. Five sensors are spread across 0.048 m, which covers the 25 mm tape with margin at any lateral offset up to about 24 mm, so the line stays visible on bends. The sensors sit 0.04 m ahead of the axle so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it. The 12 mm footprint is small enough to resolve edges and large enough to avoid dropouts. The track width of 0.12 m and the 0.03 m wheel radius give a moderate turn authority with stable yaw. The body width of 0.12 m gives an off-track limit of max(0.06, 0.0125+0.03)=0.06 m, which is a little generous. Mass 0.8 kg keeps inertia low for quick response. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with modest line error. This is a hypothesis to test, not a proven optimum.
